corroboration.reading: Every run this check refuses is already refused by the tail's own floors, so on this evidence it ADDS NO REFUSALS. And the reason is now known rather than puzzling: same-ordinal RSD correlates with whole-series per-inference RSD at Spearman 0.919 (log-log r 0.970), because a disturbance that scales a whole submission moves every dispatch inside it together. The agreement is REDUNDANCY, NOT CORROBORATION. What this module still offers that nothing else does is localisation -- see --localise -- and the fact that it refuses for a reason independent of suffix selection, which matters if a MARGINAL_TAIL's withheld median is ever published.

sensitivity.reading: The flagged count is 10 for every threshold from 11% to 20%. Flatness around the boundary is the argument for it; if this band is ever narrow, the threshold is doing the deciding and should be reported as a judgement.

localisation.character: SUBMISSION_LEVEL: most of the dispersion is whole-inference scaling — the dispatches inside an inference agreed with each other. Consistent with a clock/power excursion or queueing delay ahead of the submission.
localisation.caveat: A decomposition of the dispersion, not an independent opinion: the normalised statistic still correlates with whole-series RSD at Spearman 0.710. And like every dispersion measure it is blind to a bias that scales the whole series.

localisation.character: PER_DISPATCH: removing per-inference level barely reduces the dispersion — individual dispatches disagree on their own. Consistent with foreign work interleaved between dispatches.
localisation.caveat: A decomposition of the dispersion, not an independent opinion: the normalised statistic still correlates with whole-series RSD at Spearman 0.710. And like every dispersion measure it is blind to a bias that scales the whole series.

localisation.character: MIXED: both whole-inference scaling and per-dispatch disagreement are present in comparable measure.
